## Pull request overview Adds a new `uor-r4-proof-model` crate to the workspace to act as an executable/spec-style proof harness around key “transformerless” invariants (range bounds, deterministic top‑K ordering, Theorem 7 reverse index), plus a machine-readable proof status matrix. **Changes:** - Introduces `uor-r4-proof-model` library modules for theorem/range/top‑K proofs and a `ProofStatusMatrix`. - Adds initial unit tests exercising the proof modules. - Registers the new crate in the workspace (`Cargo.toml`) and lockfile. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 9 out of 10 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/tests/proof_model_tests.rs | Adds unit tests for proof matrix, range bounds, deterministic top‑K, Theorem 7 verification, and a zero-allocation harness. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/theorem7_proof.rs | Wraps `TransitionGraph::verify_theorem_7()` with a proof-model API and error mapping. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/range_bounds_proof.rs | Adds a checked range-bounds verifier for packed section ranges. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/proof_matrix.rs | Implements `ProofStatusMatrix` and `ProofStatus` tracking with a simple `verify_all()` gate. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/lib.rs | Exposes the crate modules. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/deterministic_topk_proof.rs | Implements canonical sorting + verification for deterministic top‑K tie-breaking. | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/src/allocation_proof.rs | Adds a “zero allocation” verification API backed by internal counters (currently not wired to actual allocations). | | crates/uor-r4-proof-model/Cargo.toml | Declares the new crate and its dependencies. | | Cargo.toml | Adds `crates/uor-r4-proof-model` as a workspace member and default-member. | | Cargo.lock | Records the new crate in the lockfile. |

review_comments.body: `verify_zero_allocation` cannot actually detect allocations as written: `ALLOC_COUNT`/`ALLOC_BYTES` are only ever stored/loaded in this module and are never incremented by a counting `#[global_allocator]` (or any other hook). As a result, `diff_count` will always be 0 and the proof will pass even when the closure performs heap allocations.

The zero-allocation test only covers a non-allocating closure, so it would still pass even if `verify_zero_allocation` fails to detect allocations. Add a negative case that performs an allocation (e.g., `Vec::push`) and assert it returns `Err`, so the harness is actually validated.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+//! Executable proof module: Packed section range boundary verification.
+
+/// Verify that packed section range `(start, len)` is strictly bounded within section length `total_len`.
review_comments.body: Doc comment says the range is "strictly bounded" within `total_len`, but the implementation allows `end == total_len` (which is typically correct for a `[start..end)` range). Consider updating the wording to match the actual contract (end <= total_len).

Keeping unused deps (especially duplicated in both dependencies and dev-dependencies) increases compile time and audit surface; consider removing until it’s actually needed.

review_comments.body: PR description/Issue #22 mention an "executable spec crate", "differential tests", and "Kani proofs", but this crate currently only adds a library (`src/lib.rs` with modules) plus unit tests—there’s no `src/main.rs`/bin target and no Kani harness/config (no `kani` references in the crate). Either add the missing executable/Kani/differential components or adjust the PR description/scope to match what’s implemented.

Fixed in the latest commit. Added a `CountingAllocator` struct that implements `GlobalAlloc` by wrapping `std::alloc::System` and calling `fetch_add` on `ALLOC_COUNT`/`ALLOC_BYTES` on every allocation. It's registered with `#[global_allocator]`, so the counters are now actually incremented on every heap allocation — `verify_zero_allocation` correctly returns `Err` when the closure allocates (verified by the existing `Vec::push` negative test case).
